evidence.note: TRACE INVERSION reframes abstention as query misalignment -- a hallucinating model answered a different (reconstructed) question than the one the user actually posed -- and detects this by reconstructing the implied query from a model's own reasoning trace and comparing it to the original via an ensemble of embedding-similarity, LLM-judged, and groundedness-detection metrics, beating five baselines in 33/36 settings across four LLMs and nine abstention datasets, while separately showing that CoT/reasoning-trace prompting itself degrades abstention accuracy by an average 2.6% versus non-reasoning prompting.
evidence.title: Answering the Wrong Question: Reasoning Trace Inversion for Abstention in LLMs
